svg.title: In the model a flash of Kenyon cells gives MBON11 a current 30 times faster than flies'; a slow current gives an EPSC close to flies' flash EPSC, and their odor EPSC's peak
svg.text: Yamada et al.'s flash, in the model: the Kenyon cell current into MBON11 is too fast
Flashed, the model's Kenyon cells fire within about 50 ms whatever their membrane time constant, so its 5 ms synapses deliver a flash's charge in about 10 ms,
peaking at 3,615 pA where flies' EPSC reaches 80-117 pA over about 250 ms. Through a slow current the same input gives an EPSC close to flies', and from the model's
Kenyon cells and depression as they are, their odor EPSC's peak (347 pA; flies about 400) and about half its plateau (83 pA; flies about 170).
